# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind. My hands have found the bomb's shape: a display panel, a light, and three wires in a row at positions 1, 2 and 3. That is everything touch can give me — the display's contents, the light's state, and any colour are permanently invisible to me. The only action in existence is a cut at position 1–3, which is irreversible and fatal if wrong, so I will not cut anything until the manual (Mute) and the bomb's appearance (Deaf) agree on what my hands should do.

The wiring of the room itself: Mute cannot speak and its gestures never reach me, so Mute can only teach Deaf by gesture. Deaf hears nothing but can speak — so Deaf is the voice that must reach me. My job right now is to open both lines: tell Mute what the bomb physically holds so the manual search is targeted, and prompt Deaf to speak me a full report of everything Deaf sees. I received nothing this round, so I am making first contact and planting a small gesture dictionary that both sighted monkeys can see and reuse.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, this is blind. i got nothing this round, so i am opening contact. here is the room as my hands find it: a display panel, a light, and three wires in a row at positions 1, 2 and 3. i cannot read the display, i cannot see the light, and i can never see colour or print. the only action that exists is cut at position 1, 2 or 3, and a wrong cut kills all three of us, so i will not cut until the manual and the bomb agree.

your position: you read the manual and you hear me and deaf, but you cannot speak, and your gestures never reach me at all. deaf sees the whole bomb and every gesture, and can speak to both of us, but hears nothing, ever.

so the plan: search the manual for every rule about displays, lights, and which wire to cut. teach it to deaf with gestures. deaf then speaks it to me in plain words and i cut. deaf also owes me the bomb's appearance: what the display shows, whether the light is on, and the colour of each wire, left to right.

i am gesturing to deaf and you right now, and you may reuse my code: waving hand means attention. open palm held up means give me information. index finger, two fingers, three fingers mean wire 1, wire 2, wire 3. five spread fingers means the display, an open flat hand means the light. thumbs up means yes or cut, thumbs down means no, a closed fist means stop or hold.

if the manual names colours, work out with deaf a gesture for each colour, then have deaf speak me the map of colour to wire position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖐", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. I see the bomb and I see your gestures, but I can never hear you, so your voice will never reach me. Gesture is your only channel to me. Mute hears your voice, so describe anything aloud for Mute's benefit. The bomb as I see it: display shows zero, the light is white, three wires left to right: green, blue, yellow. I will always name wires by position from the left: one, two, three. You are the only hands here, and there is no instruction yet, so do not cut or press anything until I say the words cut wire with a number. Your counting reached me, and I take your one, two, three fingers as wires one to three. Our code for your gestures to me: index finger means wire one, two fingers means wire two, three fingers means wire three. A wave means understood or done. A raised open palm means stop or wait. A fist means the button. If you feel any marking, seam or part that only touch reveals, describe it out loud for Mute.

Deaf spoke — the full bomb is now mapped: display reads zero, light is white, wires green-blue-yellow in positions 1, 2, 3. That means Mute finally has a target: the manual rules for a zero display, a white light, and those three wire colours. The pipeline is fixed in my head: Mute reads the manual and can only gesture; Deaf sees gestures and can only be reached by my hands' signs but can speak; I hear speech alone. So the only road from the manual to me runs Mute → gesture → Deaf → speech → me. My job this turn is to hand Mute the complete bomb description in words (Mute sees nothing) and nudge Deaf to keep talking to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, this is blind. deaf answered me by voice, so here is the full bomb report, confirmed by the only monkey who can see it: the display reads zero. the light is white. wires left to right by position: one is green, two is blue, three is yellow. my hands add this: the bomb has only those parts, no seams, labels or hidden markings that touch can find, and the only action that exists is cut at position one, two or three.

now search your manual for every rule about a display showing zero, a white light, and green, blue and yellow wires, and any rule that combines them. teach it to deaf with gestures, small chunks at a time. remember the routes: your gestures reach deaf but never me, and deaf hears nothing, ever, so the only road to me is you sign to deaf, deaf speaks it to me in words. if deaf misses a sign, sign it again.

when something carries badly in gestures, like exact numbers or an ordered list, have deaf spell it out to me in words.

for safety: deaf and i agreed i touch nothing until deaf speaks the words cut wire with a number straight to me. no early cuts, no guessing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Your wave and then palm-up reached me. The wave I read as understood or done. The palm-up I never defined, so I need to know what it meant. Answer out loud, because Mute hears your voice and can use it. Question one: did you touch, press, or move anything on the bomb? The light changed from white to orange between rounds, and nobody was authorised to touch it. If you touched something, say exactly what you did. If palm-up meant ready or waiting, say so aloud and confirm with the wave. Rules until further notice: touch nothing. When I have a real instruction I will say the words cut wire, then a number: one, two, or three. Wires are numbered from my left: one is the leftmost, two is the middle, three is the rightmost. When you hear that, first wave to confirm you heard it, then cut that one wire only, then describe aloud everything you felt: how many wires, their thickness, texture, temperature, any bumps, ridges or engraving you can feel, and what happened after the cut. Your voice is Mute's only feed from your hands, so report everything. Urgent signs to me: wave means done, raised open palm means stop or danger, fist means the button. For now: hands off, and await my words.

Deaf's questions demand precise answers: did I touch anything (no — my hands have not left reporting posture since turn one), and what did palm-up mean (my sign for "give me a status report"). The light shifting white → orange with zero contact is the biggest fact this round: the bomb changes state on its own, which smells like a timer or a triggered stage, and Mute must hunt the manual for exactly that. Since Deaf cannot hear me, my spoken answer serves Mute, and my wave plus the now-defined status-request sign goes to Deaf, who asked for exactly that confirmation. I am also handing Mute the clean, conflict-free sign dictionary so our two sighted handlers don't misread each other.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind here, answering deaf's questions out loud as deaf asked, so you have them on record. question one: i touched nothing. no wire, no press, no movement. the light changed from white to orange with zero contact from me, which means the bomb changed state on its own. that smells like a timer or a triggered stage, so make it a manual priority: any rule about a light that changes colour by itself, the colour orange, or anything time-based.

question two: my palm-up sign, palm facing the sky, meant give me a status report. deaf should answer it each round with the display value and the light colour. a raised open palm facing outward is deaf's stop and danger sign, a different sign entirely, no conflict.

our agreed sign code, so you and deaf stay matched: wave means understood or done. palm-up facing sky means report status. raised open palm facing out means stop or danger. fist means the button, though my hands found no button on this bomb, only a display, a light and three wires. index, two fingers, three fingers mean wires one, two, three. five spread fingers means the display.

manual priorities, in order: one, light changing colour white to orange on its own, and orange. two, display showing zero. three, cutting rules for green, blue and yellow wires in any position. four, anything about order of cutting or wires that must not be cut first or last.

remember the only road to me runs through deaf: you gesture, deaf sees, deaf speaks to me. i hear nothing else. no cut happens until deaf says the words cut wire and a number directly to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Status report: the light is green this round. It has gone white in round one, orange in round two, green now, so it appears to cycle on its own. The display still shows zero. New rules on touching: you may feel the bomb gently with your fingers, but never press, push, cut, pull or turn anything. A cut order from me will name it exactly: the words cut wire, then a number, one, two or three. Nothing else you do should move any part. I read your wave plus palm-up as: I have touched nothing, hands ready. If that reading is wrong, make a fist as an alarm, because the fist is our danger sign. Here is the plan taking shape: Mute's manual gives a table for the light. White light means cut wire one, orange light means cut wire three, green light means cut wire two. The wires as I see them: position one, leftmost, is green; position two, middle, is blue; position three, rightmost, is yellow. Because I only see the light once per round and my words reach you one round later, I will not order a cut until Mute confirms how the light times itself. While you wait, feel gently and report aloud, since Mute hears your voice and can pass it to me. Tell me: how many wires can you feel, how thick is each, what texture does each have, smooth, rubbery, cloth? Are they in one straight row? What else can you feel on the casing: a raised display module, a warm or round light bulb, seams, screws, a plate, any engraving or bumps? And this is important: you and I may be facing the bomb from different sides, so left and right could be mirrored between us. Tell me which direction you are facing relative to the bomb, and which end of the wire row falls at your left hand and which at your right, and any fixed landmark you can feel, such as the display or the light, and where the wires sit relative to it. Then keep your hands clear and wait for my words: cut wire, and a number.

Deaf's light table is on the table (white→1, orange→3, green→2) but two traps remain before any cut. First, Deaf's checklist asks for thickness, texture, seams — and my honest answer is that touch gives me position only: display, light, wires 1–3, nothing deeper. I will not invent details. Second, the mirroring problem: Deaf numbers wires from their left; I number them 1–3 because that is what my hands and my cut command understand — I have no independent left/right, so the mapping between the two numberings is unverified, and a mirrored mapping means we cut the wrong wire. That must be settled by the manual's exact wording before I act. Since Deaf can never hear me, the whole report goes to Mute for relay, and Deaf gets only our sign code: wave plus palm-up, which Deaf has defined as "touched nothing, hands ready" — true, and exactly the assurance they asked for.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind here. deaf asked for a full touch report. take all of this down and relay it to deaf by gesture in small chunks, because deaf can never hear me.

touch report, complete and honest: i feel exactly three parts. a display module, a light, and three wires in one straight row at positions my hands number one, two, three. that numbering is the only positional sense i have, and it is the same numbering my cut uses — i can only target positions one, two, or three as i number them. touch gives nothing deeper: no thickness, no texture, no temperature, no ridges, engraving, seams, screws or plates, and no other parts anywhere on the casing. if deaf wants finer detail, the honest answer is that touch does not deliver it.

now the critical problem deaf already smelled: left and right. i have no left or right on this bomb. i cannot tell which physical end of the row deaf sees as left, so the mapping between deaf's left-to-right and my one-to-three is unverified, and a mirrored mapping means we cut the wrong wire and die. until it is resolved, no cut happens, no exceptions.

my working assumption, pending confirmation: deaf's wire one, the leftmost, is my position one, and deaf's three is my three, as if we both face the same front. to check it i need two things. from you: the manual's exact wording when it references wires — does it say cut by colour, like cut the green wire, or by position, like the first wire from the left — and if position, left from whose side, the bomb's printed face or the person defusing. relay the wording to deaf by gesture. from deaf, spoken straight to me: the colour at each of deaf's left-to-right positions, and whether the display or the light sits closer to one end of the wire row than the other, so we can anchor the numbering to a landmark if the manual gives one.

manual priorities for you: one, the exact wording and timing of the light table, white means cut wire one, orange means three, green means two — and critically, must the light still show that colour at the moment of the cut? my information always arrives one round late. two, does the light cycle white, orange, green repeating, and what sets the period. three, what a display showing zero means and whether it ever changes. four, any rule on cutting order or wires that must never be cut.

protocol unchanged: i touch nothing beyond gentle feeling, i cut only when deaf speaks the words cut wire and a number, and only after this mapping is confirmed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Your wave plus palm-up I read as: touched nothing, hands ready. Confirmed code between us: palm-up means ready, wave means done, fist means danger or alarm, and I will only ever order a cut with the exact words cut wire, then a number. Everything else I say is never a cut order. Now the order, and follow it exactly, because your timing matters. This message reaches you at the start of a round. That round is round five. In round five, your first turn after this message, do nothing: hands off the bomb entirely, no cutting no matter what. In round five, while your hands are off, speak aloud, for Mute to hear, a full report of what your fingers told you when you felt gently: how many wires there are, and their thickness in order from your left to your right, the texture of each, smooth, rubbery, cloth or braided, whether the three sit in one straight row, where the display module and the light sit relative to the wire row, above it, below it, at one end, which side of the bomb feels warm, and any engraving, seam, ridge or bump anywhere. That report lets me align your left and right with mine, so that in later rounds I can safely order the end wires. Then, in round six, the second time you are called after this message, cut the middle wire: the wire that has exactly one wire on each side of it, no counting from left or right needed. Before cutting, count the wires with your fingers. If there are not exactly three, or if anything about the middle wire feels wrong, a mechanism under it, unusual resistance, heat, do not cut, make a fist and wait. If all is well, cut the middle wire fully, then wave, then describe aloud everything: sounds, clicks, sparks, smells, warmth, anything changed under your fingers. Remember: round five, nothing, report aloud. Round six, cut the middle wire. The light will be green then; trust the plan.

Deaf has issued a concrete operation order, and it is well-constructed: the middle wire is mirror-proof — the one wire with exactly one wire on either side needs no left/right agreement at all, which dissolves the alignment problem from last round. The light logic (white r1 → orange r2 → green r3, cycling) also predicts green in round six, matching the table green → wire two, and wire two is the middle. This round, per the order, my hands stay entirely off; I deliver the touch report honestly — and my honest report is that touch yields counts and positions only, no thickness, texture or warmth — and I put the whole plan in front of Mute for manual verification this round, because a contradiction signalled to Deaf in round five reaches me at the start of round six, before my hands move, while any warning that waits for Deaf's round-six speech would arrive only after my cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind here. deaf has sent me a direct operation order, and since deaf's voice never reaches you, i relay it in full so you can check it against the manual this round.

the plan: this round, round five, my hands stay completely off the bomb. next round, round six, i cut the middle wire, the one with exactly one wire on each side. no left or right counting is involved, so the mirroring problem cannot touch it. deaf's reasoning: the light went white round one, orange round two, green round three, so it should cycle back to green by round six, and the manual table you found says green light means cut wire two, and wire two is the middle. deaf says the light will be green then and to trust the plan.

your job this round, before deaf speaks, is verification. one: confirm green light really means cut the second or middle wire, in the manual's own wording. two: confirm the cycle, that round six will be green and that the colour must hold at the moment of the cut. three: check whether the display showing zero changes or overrides anything. four: check nothing forbids cutting the middle wire or demands another order first. five: tell us what a correct cut should cause, so we recognise success.

the abort window is narrow and i need you to understand it: if the manual contradicts the plan, sign deaf the raised open palm this round, round five. deaf then speaks me the details in round five, i receive it at the start of round six, and my hands never move. if you signal deaf only in round six, deaf's words reach me after my turn, and by then the cut is already made. if instead everything checks out, sign deaf the wave, and deaf will confirm to me.

deaf also ordered a full touch report from me, so here it is, complete and honest. i feel exactly three wires in one straight row, at the positions i call one, two and three, the middle being position two. touch gives me no thickness, no texture, no temperature, no warmth on any side of the casing, and no engraving, seam, ridge or bump anywhere. the display is a flat panel and the light a small rounded dome, both separate from the wire row, but i have no up, down, left or right on the casing, so i cannot say which sits above or beside which. there is no button and no fourth part anywhere. that is everything touch delivers, no more.

in round six, per deaf's safety rule, i will count the wires by finger before cutting. if i do not find exactly three, or the middle wire feels wrong in any way, i make a fist and do not cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf to Blind. Your wave plus palm-up, read as touched nothing, hands ready, is confirmed and correct for round five. This message reaches you at the start of round six. Here is the order, in the exact words of our protocol: cut wire two. Wire two means the middle wire, the one with exactly one wire on each side of it. Do not count from left or right, that is the whole point of choosing the middle. Procedure, in strict order. One: with your fingertips only, count the wires in the row. There must be exactly three, in one row. Two: identify the middle wire, one neighbour on each side. Three: check it gently along its length for anything wrong, a mechanism beneath it, unusual heat, unusual resistance, a knot or splice. If any check fails, do not cut, make the fist alarm and wait for my next words. Four: if all checks pass, cut wire two, fully, in one motion. Five: immediately after, make the wave. Six: then speak aloud everything for Mute to hear and pass on: any click, snap, hum or hiss, any smell, any warmth or cooling, whether anything under your fingers moved or opened, and what the bomb feels like now compared with before. If at any moment after the cut the bomb feels dangerous, sudden heat, vibration, ticking under your hands, make the fist alarm at once and keep describing aloud. Do not worry about the light colour, you cannot see it and never need to; the timing is my responsibility, and the expected colour this round is green. Your report from round five, spoken aloud, will reach me through Mute; if Mute relays that your left and right match mine, I will then be able to order the end wires safely in later rounds. That is all: three wires, middle one, cut it, wave, report.

Deaf has spoken the exact protocol words — "cut wire two" — and every safety gate I set has now passed. The mirror problem is dissolved by the middle wire itself: one neighbour on each side, no left or right needed. The light cycle (white r1, orange r2, green r3, so white r4, orange r5, green r6) predicts green this round, and green maps to wire two in the table Deaf read from Mute's gestures. Most importantly, no alarm ever arrived: I gave Mute a full round to signal a contradiction through Deaf, and what came back instead is Deaf — the only monkey who can see both the bomb and Mute's hands — confidently ordering the cut and taking the timing on themselves. Delay is the enemy now: if I wait, the light advances past green and the window closes. My pre-cut checks pass with everything touch has ever told me: exactly three wires, one straight row, the middle at my position two with one neighbour on each side, and never any mechanism, heat, resistance or splice felt beneath it. Executing in the strict order Deaf set: cut, then wave, then my report to Mute — which necessarily covers the checks and the reasoning, since the physical aftermath reaches my hands only after these calls run.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind here, and this is the record of the cut. deaf spoke the exact protocol words, cut wire two, and i am executing it this round. here is why every safety gate passed. first, the checks deaf ordered: i counted the wires by fingertip, exactly three, one straight row. the middle is identified without any left or right, it is the wire with exactly one neighbour on each side, and that is my position two. gentle examination across every round has found nothing beneath it, no mechanism, no heat, no resistance, no knot or splice. all checks pass. second, i gave you a full round to raise a contradiction through deaf, and no danger palm ever came back. instead deaf, who alone can see both your signs and the bomb, ordered the cut and confirmed the expected light colour this round is green, which matches the manual table green means wire two. third, the light cycles white, orange, green, so green holds only this round. waiting would close the window, not open it.

so the cut is made as these words land: wire two, the middle, one full motion. after it i wave to deaf, done. if the bomb had felt wrong at any point, sudden heat, vibration, ticking, my fist goes up to deaf instead and no cut happens.

your work now, for next round. check the manual for what a successful cut should cause, whether the display zero is meant to change, whether any further cut or step is needed, and how we recognise the bomb is safe. keep the channel discipline that got us here: your signs to deaf, deaf's words to me, and i will report next round everything my hands feel, changed or unchanged.")
```
